To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

basal adenosine modulated the functional properties of postsynaptic AMPA receptors in the hippocampus by activating multiple ARs, A1R, A2AR and possibly A3R, with different effects on glutamatergc transmission.
adenosine acting on A1R and/or A3R decreases, while acting on A2AR increases the amplitude of AMPA currents in hippocampi neurons.

the activation of different adenosine receptors by basal adenosinergic tone in the hippocampus has opposite effects on AMPA receptors function, reducing or enhancing glutamatergics currents, respectively, through the modulation of GluR1 subunit phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neuromodulating action of adenosinergic system, which is known to be involved in many brain pathologies, and in particular, in the modulation of synaptic activity.
the study of the mechanisms by which extracellular adenosinergic tone modulates synaptic transmission in the hippocampus.
the role of basal adenosine in the modulation of synaptic plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
basal adenosine modulate AMPA receptors function through the activation of multiple ARs.
basal adenosine modulate the functional properties of glutamateric currents in hippocampus through the activation of different adenosine receptor subtypes.
the activation of A2A adenosine receptors, by means of an increase of the basal extracellular concentration of adenosine, can potentiate glutamatergics transmission in the hippocampus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
basal extracellular adenosinergic tone is able to modulate the properties of AMPA glutamatergics receptors through the activation of multiple ARs.
basal levels of adenosine in the brain are able to modulate synaptic transmission by acting on multiple AR subtypes.
the basal extracellular adenosinergic tone modulates AMPA currents in hippocampi through the activation of different AR subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
basal levels of adenosine modulate the functional properties of the AMPA receptor, acting on both GluR1 subunit phosphorylation and channel gating.
adenosine modulating glutamatergics synapses is not only a mechanism to reduce synaptic transmission in pathological conditions but also a physiological process.

basal adenosine levels modulate the functional properties of hippocampal AMPA receptors through the activation of multiple adrenergic receptors (ARs), which in turn affect GluR1 Ser-845 phosphorylation.
